label: Sixth-edition aphorisms
title: Aphorism § 187
text:
§ 187



But those affections, alterations and ailments appearing on the
          external parts, that do not arise from any external injury or that have only some slight
          external wound for their immediate exciting cause, are produced in quite another manner;
          their source lies in some internal malady. To consider them as mere local affections, and
          at the same time to treat them only, or almost only, as it were surgically, with topical
          applications - as the old school have done from the remotest ages - is as absurd as it is
          pernicious in its results.
